races.title: State House, District 96
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Park Inglefield
cands.bio: Democratic nominee for NC House District 96 in 2026. Born in Statesville and raised in Hickory. Political science graduate of Northeastern University. Worked in public service and training women to run for office in Boston, then as Deputy State Director for Rise Free. Now North Carolina State Director for Young People's Alliance.

endorsements.text: Equality NC (self-reported in her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey)
Voter guide recommendations from the Sway voting groups Fair Map Fight Club and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy

cands.gaps: We found no record of Park Inglefield holding elected office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no stated positions on homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, abortion, or teacher pay. We could not confirm her birth year or the year she left North Carolina for Boston. The sources differ on which high school she attended. No pages beyond her Ballotpedia profile and her campaign site were available.

local.label: Roots 100: She says she was born in Statesville and raised in Hickory, attended Hickory public schools, and returned to North Carolina in 2022 after about ten years in Boston.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: She spent ten years in Boston in public service and training women to run for office. Since 2022 she has been Deputy State Director for Rise Free and then North Carolina State Director for Young People's Alliance, where she organizes on AI regulation policy. She served a year on the Catawba Grand Jury. She has held no elected office.
qual.why: Her record is a policy-advocacy and nonprofit management career, which fits the middle band. She has no legislative service or budget work, so she scores below the top band.
qual.label: Her record is a policy-advocacy and nonprofit management career, which fits the middle band. She has no legislative service or budget work, so she scores below the top band.

stop-data-centers.evidence: In her Ballotpedia survey she said she is passionate about protecting natural resources from overdevelopment and the rapid spread of data centers. She also said the AI boom needs regulation and oversight to avoid diminishing natural resources. She did not call for a statewide ban or preemption.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: In her Ballotpedia survey she said she wants to protect and preserve natural resources from overdevelopment. She also listed defending natural resources among her campaign priorities and said she wants government to work for residents rather than developers.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In her Ballotpedia survey she said she will work to ensure vouchers go to families that truly need them and to fully fund public schools. She criticized government support for private schools going to ultra-wealthy families.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

roots.summary: She says she was born in Statesville and raised in Hickory, attended Hickory public schools, and returned to North Carolina in 2022 after about ten years in Boston.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Said she is passionate about "protecting and preserving our natural resources from overdevelopment and the rapid spread of data centers," and that without regulation the AI boom risks diminishing natural resources.

Named protecting natural resources from overdevelopment as a policy passion and said she wants a legacy of government working for residents, "not developers, not special interests." Also named strain from rapid population growth on energy, housing and water as the state's greatest challenge.

cands.name: Jay Adams
cands.bio: Republican member of the North Carolina House for District 96 (Catawba County) since 2015. Commercial real estate broker in Hickory with a Citadel B.S. in education. Earlier worked for SIECOR as a technical communications specialist and for Deville Furniture.
cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace city or where he grew up. The pages we had did not list the contents of the bills he has sponsored, so we could not confirm anything he has done on data centers, homestead property taxes, land purchases by out-of-state or foreign buyers, growth limits, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns or abortion. We found no statements from him on those topics, and no documented stance on data centers or development. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or endorsements. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in recent cycles. His campaign website appears to date from the 2020 election cycle.

local.label: Roots 55: His campaign site calls him a North Carolina native who has lived in Hickory since 1975, and Wikipedia also says he has lived in Hickory since 1975; where he grew up is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since January 2015 and sat on Appropriations committees. Licensed real estate broker since 1983 with a career in commercial real estate, and a former technical communications specialist at SIECOR.
qual.why: More than a decade of legislative service plus a long business career as a broker and small business owner. Committee seats and local civic boards were not counted.
qual.label: More than a decade of legislative service plus a long business career as a broker and small business owner. Committee seats and local civic boards were not counted.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Wrote on his campaign site that families should have educational options, whether a private school, charter school, magnet school or home schooling. This statement comes from his 2020-cycle site.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)
